liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Black Queen** (2 reviews, 1 other source): First Black Queen since December 1969, and the last one ever played; Black Queen was played by the Dead only twice [5][27][36]
- **Iko Iko** (2 reviews): Black Queen and Iko Iko especially impressed this listener; Stephen Stills came out for Iko Iko [31][34]
- **Looks Like Rain** (1 review): Jerry's guitar work on this song is singled out as classic [30]
- **Truckin'** (1 review): China Cat, Rider, Uncle John's and Truckin' opening set two felt like a greatest-hits package; Stills then joined [35]
- **The Other One** (1 review): The Other One was incredible; Stills joined for Black Queen and Iko Iko [37]

## Setlist highlights

- **Touch Of Grey, Set Break**: cut on the recording [1]

## The recordings

- **gd1983-04-16.132874.SBD.Keo.Flac1644** (recommended): soundboard; 25 songs; 160 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [1]
- **gd83-04-16.sbd.fink.14940.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 22 songs; 165 min; rated 3.29/5 by 7 [4]. Said about its sound: Tape hiss is noticeable on this soundboard recording [30]
- **gd1983-04-16.175517.sbd.bradt.miller.flac2496**: soundboard; 22 songs; 161 min [5]
- **gd1983-04-16.162704.senn421.blend.vita.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 22 songs; 156 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [7]
- **gd1983-04-16.153497.m160.miller.flac2496**: source not stated; 23 songs; 155 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [13]

## Around the show

- Stephen Stills, playing nearby, stopped in at both nights' shows [27]
- Stephen Stills appeared as a surprise special guest at the Brendan Byrne show [31]
- Stephen Stills guested, sitting in on Black Queen [32]
- On the second night Stills sang a song about loving the one you're with [34]
- Stills added extra spice toward the end of the show [38]
- Stills played guitar and sang from Black Queen > Iko Iko, and on Black Peter through the end [5]
- Stills guested on Black Queen, Iko Iko, Black Peter, One More Saturday Night and Johnny B. Goode [7]
- Venue security could be heard freaking out over the tapers as the show started [13]
- The next night was a sluggish contrast, with a long Black Peter, as if the band were hungover [34]
- People speculated whether Stills would return the next night; he did [37]
- Tempos ran fast and uptempo on older tunes, with Touch of Grey perhaps too fast [38]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1983-04-16.132874.SBD.Keo.Flac1644**: transferred by Keo; source: Soundboard Master Cassettes > (Unk) Reel To Reel > Low Gen PCM Early 90's > Sony HG L750 Beta Tape > Sony SL2405 Beta VCR > Modified PCM601ESD > SPDIF > VX… [1]. Also: Shared by a friend; first set may be an upgrade avoiding CDR and EAC generations, with some tape hiss [1]
- **gd83-04-16.sbd.fink.14940.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Jeff Williams and Alan J Fink; source: Soundboard [4]
- **gd1983-04-16.175517.sbd.bradt.miller.flac2496**: taped by Thanks to Bill Bradt and Kathy Weir Bradt for the tapes; transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  December 9, 2025; source: Set 1: SBD > Cassette Master > Cassette (dbx) Set 2: SBD > Cassette Master (TDK MA-R90) [5]. Also: Tapes came from Bill Bradt and Kathy Weir Bradt; tracking issues made Bird Song unusable [5]
- **gd1983-04-16.162704.senn421.blend.vita.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Jim Vita; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Jim Vita's Master (FOB) Audience Cassettes; 3 x Sennheiser 421 mics (15th row, center) > unknown mixer > Sony D5M (Maxell XLII-S) [7]
- **gd1983-04-16.153497.m160.miller.flac2496**: taped by Recorded by Charlie Miller; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: (FOB) Beyer M160 > Cassette Master (Sony WM-D6C/Maxell UDXL-II/Dolby B) [13]. Also: Recorded five feet in front of the soundboard, ten feet left; batteries died during Black Peter, last three songs patched afterward; Set 1 comes from a first-generation copy of the master made in 1990 for a friend [13]

citations.title: April 16, 1983

claims.text: Stephen Stills, playing nearby, stopped in at both nights' shows
First Black Queen since December 1969, and the last one ever played
Tape hiss is noticeable on this soundboard recording
Jerry's guitar work on this song is singled out as classic
Stephen Stills appeared as a surprise special guest at the Brendan Byrne show
Black Queen and Iko Iko especially impressed this listener
Stephen Stills guested, sitting in on Black Queen
Stephen Stills came out for Iko Iko
The next night was a sluggish contrast, with a long Black Peter, as if the band were hungover
On the second night Stills sang a song about loving the one you're with
China Cat, Rider, Uncle John's and Truckin' opening set two felt like a greatest-hits package; Stills then joined
Black Queen was played by the Dead only twice
The Other One was incredible; Stills joined for Black Queen and Iko Iko
People speculated whether Stills would return the next night; he did
Tempos ran fast and uptempo on older tunes, with Touch of Grey perhaps too fast
Stills added extra spice toward the end of the show
Shared by a friend; first set may be an upgrade avoiding CDR and EAC generations, with some tape hiss
Tapes came from Bill Bradt and Kathy Weir Bradt; tracking issues made Bird Song unusable
Stills played guitar and sang from Black Queen > Iko Iko, and on Black Peter through the end
First performance since December 10, 1969, and its last time played
Master cassettes from Jim Vita, transferred by Charlie Miller; Sennheiser 421 source patches 28 seconds of Drums
Stills guested on Black Queen, Iko Iko, Black Peter, One More Saturday Night and Johnny B. Goode
Recorded five feet in front of the soundboard, ten feet left; batteries died during Black Peter, last three songs patched afterward
Venue security could be heard freaking out over the tapers as the show started
Set 1 comes from a first-generation copy of the master made in 1990 for a friend
